source_text: Πλὴν καὶ τότε ταῖς λύπαις ὅρον καὶ μέτρον ἐπιτιθεὶς, καὶ ταῖς εὐσεβέσιν ἐκείναις φωναῖς κοσμῶν τὸ γινόμενον, ἔλεγεν· Ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν, ὁ Κύριος ἀφείλετο· ὡς τῷ Κυρίῳ ἔδοξεν, οὕτω καὶ ἐγένετο, μονονουχὶ τοιαῦτα βοῶν· Ἐκλήθην πατὴρ ἐφ' ὅσον ὁ τοῦτό με ποιήσας ἐβούλετο χρόνον. Περιελεῖν μου τὸν ἐκ τῆς γονῆς στέφανον ἐβουλεύσατο πάλιν, οὐ διαμάχομαι περὶ τῶν ἰδίων αὐτῷ. Κρατείτω τὸ τῷ Δεσπότῃ δοκοῦν· αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ πλάστης τοῦ γένους, ἐγὼ δὲ ὄργανον. Τί με χρὴ δοῦλον ὄντα δυσχεραίνειν ἀνόνητα, καὶ μέμφεσθαι ψῆφον ἣν οὐ δύναμαι λύειν; Τοιούτοις τὸν διάβολον ὁ δίκαιος κατηκόντιζε ῥή μασιν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ αὐτὸν νικῶντα εἶδε πάλιν ὁ δυσμενὴς, καὶ οὐδενὶ τούτων τιναχθῆναι δυνάμενον, αὐτῇ τῇ σαρκὶ τὸ τῆς πείρας προσῆγε μηχάνημα, καὶ τὸ σῶμα μαστίξας ἀῤῥήτοις πληγαῖς, σκωλήκων ἀνα δίδοσθαι πηγὰς ἐξ αὐτοῦ παρεσκεύασε· καὶ τῶν τῆς βασιλείας θρόνων τὸν ἄνδρα καταγαγὼν, ἐπὶ κοπρίας ἐκάθισεν. Ὁ δὲ, καὶ τοιούτοις βαλλόμενος πάθεσιν, ἀκίνητος ἔμεινε· καὶ σπαραττομένου τοῦ σώματος, ἄσυλον ἐφύλαττε τὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας θησαυρὸν ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ τῆς ψυχῆς. Οὐκ ἔχων τοίνυν ὅ τι ποιήσει λοιπὸν ὁ πολέμιος, ἐπὶ τὴν τῆς ἀρχαίας ἐπιβουλῆς ἔρχεται μνήμην, καὶ τὴν τοῦ γυναίου διάνοιαν ὑπο σύρας εἰς ἀσεβῆ γνώμην καὶ βλάσφημον, δι' ἐκείνης σαλεύειν ἐπειρᾶτο τὸν ἀθλητήν. Καὶ ἡ μὲν πρὸς τὸν μακρὸν χρόνον ἀπαγορεύσασα, τῷ δικαίῳ παρίστατο, κάτω νενευκυῖα, καὶ τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοῖς ὁρωμένοις συγκρούουσα, καὶ τοὺς τῆς εὐσε βείας αὐτῷ καρποὺς ὀνειδίζουσα, καὶ καταλέγουσα μὲν τὴν παλαιὰν εὐθηνίαν τῶν οἰκείων, ὑποδεικνύουσα δὲ τὰ παρόντα κακὰ, καὶ οἷον ἐξ οἵων ἔλαχε βίον, καὶ τίνα τῶν πολλῶν θυσιῶν ἐδέξατο παρὰ τοῦ Δεσπότου μισθὸν, ἔλεγέ τε ἀεὶ τῆς μὲν τῶν γυναικῶν ὀλιγο ψυχίας ἄξια ῥήματα, ταράξαι δὲ πάντα ἄνδρα δυνά μενα, καὶ περιτρέψαι καὶ γενναίαν διάνοιαν· πλανῆ τις γὰρ καὶ λάτρις περιέρχομαι, ἡ βασιλὶς δουλεύω, καὶ πρὸς τὰς τῶν ἐμῶν οἰκετῶν χεῖρας ἠνάγκασμαι βλέπειν, καὶ τρέφουσα πάλαι πολλοὺς, ἀγαπητῶς ἐκ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων παρατρέφομαι νῦν· καὶ ὅτι καλὸν εἴη καὶ χρήσιμον, ἀσεβέσι χρησάμενον ῥήμασιν ἑαυτὸν τῆς γῆς ἐκτεμεῖν, τὸ τῆς τοῦ κτίσαντος ὀργῆς ἀκονήσαντα ξίφος, ἢ διακαρτεροῦντα πρὸς τὰ δεινὰ, τὸν ἐν τοῖς ἀγῶσι μόχθον ἑαυτῷ καὶ τῇ συνοικούσῃ μηκύνειν. Ὁ δὲ, ἐπὶ τούτοις τοῖς ῥήμασιν ἀχθεσθεὶς, ὡς ἐπ' οὐδενὶ τῶν προτέρων κακῶν, καὶ θυμοῦ τὸ βλέμμα πληρώσας, καὶ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα καθάπερ πρὸς πολεμίαν ἀποστραφεὶς, τί φησιν; Ἵνα τί ὡς μία τῶν ἀφρόνων γυναικῶν ἐφθέγξω; Κατάθου, φησὶν, ὦ γύναι, τὴν συμβουλήν. Μέχρι τίνος τὴν κοινὴν ἐν οἷς λέγεις ὑβρίζεις ζωήν; Ἐψεύσω καὶ τὴν ἐμὴν, ὡς οὐκ ηὐ χόμην, ἀναστροφὴν, διέβαλες ἐν οἷς ἐλάλησας καὶ τὸν ἐμὸν βίον. Ἐξ ἡμισείας ἠσεβηκέναι νενόμικα νῦν, ἐπειδήπερ ἓν μὲν σῶμα ἀμφοτέρους ἡμᾶς ὁ γάμος ἐποίησε, σὺ δὲ εἰς βλασφημίαν κατέπεσες. Εἰ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἐδεξάμεθα ἐκ χειρὸς Κυρίου, τὰ κακὰ οὐχ ὑποίσομεν; Ἀνάμνησον τῶν φθασάντων σεαυτὴν ἀγαθῶν. Ἀντισήκωσον τὰ κρείττω τοῖς χείροσιν. Οὐδενὸς ἀνθρώπων ὁ βίος διόλου μακάριος.
thought_title: Job's wife tempts him and Job rebukes her
orientation: Basil is retelling Job's trials: after Job endured the loss of his children and his body was struck with sores, the devil now uses Job's wife to tempt him to blaspheme.
pass_a_gloss: Yet even then, setting a limit and measure to his griefs, and adorning what was happening with those pious words, he said: 'The Lord gave, the Lord has taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it happened,' all but crying out such things as these: 'I was called father for as long a time as the one who made me this willed. He willed to strip from me again the crown from offspring; I do not fight about what belongs to him. Let what seems good to the Master prevail; he is the fashioner of the race, and I am an instrument. Why must I, being a slave, be vexed to no profit, and find fault with a verdict which I cannot undo?' With such words the righteous man was striking down the devil. But when the hostile one saw him again winning, and able to be shaken by none of these things, he brought the device of trial to the very flesh, and having scourged the body with unspeakable blows, he caused springs of worms to be given forth from it; and having brought the man down from the thrones of the kingdom, he seated him on a dung heap. But he, though struck with such sufferings, remained unmoved; and while the body was being torn, he kept the treasure of piety inviolate in the hidden place of the soul. Therefore the enemy, not having what he would do next, comes to the memory of the ancient plot, and having dragged down the thought of the woman into an impious and blasphemous opinion, through her he was trying to shake the athlete. And she, having given up because of the long time, stood beside the righteous man, bowed down, and striking her hands together over what was seen, and reproaching him with the fruits of his piety, and recounting the old prosperity of the household, and pointing out the present evils, and what sort of life from what sort of things she had obtained, and what reward for the many sacrifices she had received from the Master, she kept saying words worthy of the faintheartedness of women, but able to trouble every man and to overturn even a noble mind: 'For I wander about as a vagabond and a menial servant; I, the queen, am a slave, and I have been forced to look to the hands of my own household servants, and though formerly feeding many, I am now barely fed from the goods of others; and that it would be good and useful, having used impious words, to cut oneself out of the earth, having sharpened the sword of the anger of the creator, or, enduring against the terrible things, to prolong the toil in the contests for oneself and for the wife living with him.' But he, grieved at these words as at none of the former evils, and having filled his glance with anger, and having turned to the woman as to an enemy, what does he say? 'Why have you spoken as one of the foolish women? Put away, he says, O woman, the counsel. Until when do you insult the common life in what you say? You have lied about my conduct, as I would not have wished; you have slandered my life in what you have said. I have now considered that I have acted impiously by half, since indeed marriage made us both one body, but you have fallen into blasphemy. If we received the good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not endure the bad things? Remind yourself of the good things that came before. Weigh the better things against the worse. No human being's life is altogether blessed.'

choices.why: πλάστης means molder or fashioner; 'race' for γένος keeps the sense of the human family or offspring, matching Job's context of losing his children.
ὄργανον is a tool or instrument; Job contrasts himself as a passive tool with God as the active fashioner.
μηχάνημα is a contrivance or device; πεῖρα here is trial or testing, matching the devil's assault on Job's body.
ἄρρητος means unutterable or unspeakable; πληγαῖς are blows or strokes, conveying the severity of Job's bodily affliction.
κοπρία is a dung heap or manure pile, the traditional place where Job sat in his affliction.
ἀθλητής is an athlete or contestant; Basil uses the athletic image for Job's contest of endurance against the devil.

pass_b_english: Yet even then he set a limit and a measure to his grief, and he adorned what was happening with those devout words. He said, 'The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it has happened' (Job 1:21). He was all but crying out: 'I was called a father for as long as the One who made me so willed. He has chosen to strip away the crown from my offspring again; I do not fight over what belongs to Him. Let the Master's will prevail. He is the fashioner of the race, and I am an instrument. Why should I, a servant, be pointlessly distressed and find fault with a verdict I cannot overturn?' With such words the righteous man was striking the devil down with darts. But when the enemy saw that he was victorious again and could not be shaken by any of these things, he brought the device of trial against his very flesh. He scourged his body with unspeakable blows and made springs of worms pour out from it. He brought the man down from the thrones of his kingdom and seated him on a dung heap. Yet even when struck by such sufferings, Job remained unmoved. While his body was being torn, he kept the treasure of his devotion inviolate in the hidden place of his soul. So the enemy, having nothing left to do, returned to the memory of his ancient plot. He dragged down the woman's mind into an impious and blasphemous resolve, and through her he tried to shake the athlete. She, despairing at the long duration, stood before the righteous man, bent down, striking her hands together at what she saw, reproaching him for the fruits of his devotion. She recounted the old prosperity of their household and pointed to the present evils—what a life he had received from what circumstances, and what reward he had received from the Master for his many sacrifices. She kept saying words worthy of women's faintheartedness, but capable of troubling any man and overturning even a noble mind: 'I wander about as a vagabond and a menial servant. I who was a queen am a slave, and I am forced to look to the hands of my own household servants. I who once fed many am now glad just to be fed from what belongs to others.' And she said that it would be good and useful to use impious words and cut himself off from the earth, sharpening the sword of the Creator's wrath, or, by enduring the horrors, to prolong the labor of the contest for himself and the woman who lived with him. But he was grieved by these words as by none of his earlier evils. His gaze filled with anger, and he turned to the woman as if to an enemy. What does he say? 'Why have you spoken like one of the foolish women? Put away your counsel, woman. How long will you insult the life we share by what you say? You have misrepresented my conduct in a way I never wished. You have slandered my life by what you have spoken. I now consider myself half guilty of impiety, since marriage made the two of us one body, and you have fallen into blasphemy. If we received good things from the Lord's hand, shall we not endure the bad?' (Job 2:10). Remember the good things that came to you before. Weigh the better things against the worse. No human being's life is entirely blessed.

problems.why: ηὐχόμην means 'I lived/practiced', not 'prayed'; sense is 'as I did not live'
problems.fix: which was not how I lived

problems.quote: He has chosen to strip away the crown of my children again
problems.source_quote: Περιελεῖν μου τὸν ἐκ τῆς γονῆς στέφανον ἐβουλεύσατο πάλιν
problems.why: ἐκ τῆς γονῆς means 'from my offspring/progeny', not 'of my children'; γονή = offspring, not children specifically
problems.fix: He has chosen to strip away the crown from my offspring again

problems.quote: She had given up over the long time
problems.source_quote: ἡ μὲν πρὸς τὸν μακρὸν χρόνον ἀπαγορεύσασα
problems.why: ἀπαγορεύω means 'given up' as in 'despaired/yielded,' but the phrase is unclear; she had been worn down by the long time.
problems.fix: She, worn down by the long time
problems.ruling: ἀπαγορεύσασα means 'despaired/gave up,' but 'given up over the long time' is ungrammatical and unclear; she despaired at the long duration.

problems.quote: what reward he had gotten from the Master for his many sacrifices
problems.source_quote: τίνα τῶν πολλῶν θυσιῶν ἐδέξατο παρὰ τοῦ Δεσπότου μισθόν
problems.why: This is the wife's speech about Job, not about 'he'; she asks what reward Job received for his many sacrifices.
problems.fix: what reward he had received from the Master for his many sacrifices
problems.ruling: τίνα...μισθόν is the wife's rhetorical question 'what reward,' but English 'he had gotten' makes it a statement about Job, changing grammar and force.

fixed: ηὐχόμην is imperfect of εὔχομαι, but in this context it means 'I lived/practiced' (as in a way of life), not 'prayed'; the English 'which I never prayed for' misstates the source, so changed to 'which was not how I lived'.
ἐκ τῆς γονῆς means 'from my offspring/progeny', not 'of my children'; γονή is offspring, not specifically children, so changed to 'from my offspring'.

ἀπαγορεύω here means 'to be worn down/despair' over the long time, not simply 'given up'; the phrase πρὸς τὸν μακρὸν χρόνον indicates being worn down by the long time, so changed to 'She, worn down by the long time'.
The source has ἐδέξατο (aorist middle), 'received', not 'had gotten'; the English 'had gotten' is too colloquial and slightly off, so changed to 'had received'.

problems.quote: She, worn down by the long time, and she stood before the righteous man
problems.source_quote: Καὶ ἡ μὲν πρὸς τὸν μακρὸν χρόνον ἀπαγορεύσασα, τῷ δικαίῳ παρίστατο
problems.why: 'ἀπαγορεύσασα' means 'giving up/desponding', not 'worn down'; 'πρὸς τὸν μακρὸν χρόνον' = 'at the long time' i.e., despairing of the long duration. 'and she stood' is redundant and ungrammatical.
problems.fix: She, despairing at the long duration, stood before the righteous man

problems.quote: what a life he had received in exchange for what he had before
problems.source_quote: καὶ οἷον ἐξ οἵων ἔλαχε βίον
problems.why: 'ἔλαχε' means 'he obtained/received by lot', but 'ἐξ οἵων' = 'from what circumstances', not 'in exchange for what'; the phrase means 'what a life from what circumstances he received'.
problems.fix: what a life he had received from what circumstances

problems.quote: You have lied about my conduct, which was not how I lived
problems.source_quote: Ἐψεύσω καὶ τὴν ἐμὴν, ὡς οὐκ ηὐχόμην, ἀναστροφήν
problems.why: 'ὡς οὐκ ηὐχόμην' = 'as I did not pray/wish' or 'contrary to my prayer', not 'which was not how I lived'; 'ηὐχόμην' is from 'εὔχομαι' (pray, wish), not from a word meaning 'live'. This misreads the verb entirely.
problems.fix: You have lied about my conduct, contrary to my prayer

problems.quote: rather than enduring the horrors and prolonging the labor of the contest for himself and for the woman who lived with him
problems.source_quote: ἢ διακαρτεροῦντα πρὸς τὰ δεινά, τὸν ἐν τοῖς ἀγῶσι μόχθον ἑαυτῷ καὶ τῇ συνοικούσῃ μηκύνειν
problems.why: 'ἢ' = 'or' (not 'rather than'—this is her proposal, not a comparison); 'διακαρτεροῦντα' = 'enduring'; 'τὸν ἐν τοῖς ἀγῶσι μόχθον... μηκύνειν' = 'to prolong the labor of the contests'. The 'rather than' makes it seem like Job's choice, but it's her argument: 'or, by enduring the horrors, to prolong...'
problems.fix: or, by enduring the horrors, to prolong the labor of the contest for himself and the woman who lived with him
problems.ruling: ἤ = 'or' presenting wife's alternative proposal, not 'rather than' comparison. Changes her argument's structure and meaning.

dismissed.note: 'He has chosen' is a fair rendering of the middle verb ἐβουλεύσατο, and 'crown from my offspring' gives the sense; the checker's grammar point is wrong.

dismissed.quote: I do not fight over what belongs to Him
dismissed.why: τῶν ἰδίων means 'my own things/possessions', not 'what belongs to Him'; αὐτῷ is dative of reference 'with him'
dismissed.note: τῶν ἰδίων αὐτῷ can fairly mean 'what is his own' (the children were God's gift), which fits Job's point; 'my own possessions' is not required.
